Use the Japandi / Japandi RM100k / Wabi-Sabi buttons to compare. The RM100k version keeps the layout, colours and kitchen island. It uses flat sage laminate doors instead of painted shaker, a simpler bought bed, and a fluted TV panel instead of the full slat wall. It has no window seat or terrace bench, and tiled bathrooms instead of microcement.

Wabi-Sabi idea

Clay plasterHand-troweled walls
Smoked oakAll joinery
Charred timberCeiling beams
Clay microcementFloors
TerracottaClay vessels
River stoneSide tables

Same layout, but it celebrates natural, aged and imperfect materials instead of crisp finishes. The walls are hand-troweled clay or lime plaster, with seamless clay-tone microcement on the floors. The joinery is plain smoked oak with no shaker frames, and dark timber beams run across the living, dining and master ceilings. Furniture is rougher: a second bench replaces the dining chairs, river stones serve as side tables, and terracotta vessels hold dry branches. It costs more mainly because of the plaster and microcement. For a cheaper version, use limewash paint and warm stone-look vinyl.

Japandi material palette

Room by room · clear size, mm

    Design idea. One continuous light-oak floor ties living, dining and the bedrooms together, so the long narrow plan reads as one calm space. Dark walnut and charcoal pieces sit low and are kept few. Paper lanterns give warm, soft light, and plants and the terrace bring in green. Storage is built in full-height so surfaces stay clear. All doors are solid fir in slim grey frames, the entrance has fir double doors, and the terrace door is a grey-framed glass slider.

    Accuracy. Room sizes are scaled from the image (±100 mm). Furniture sizes are standard catalogue sizes. Check door swings against the final dimensioned plan.
